Parameters (D-014d): supply T: SH 35 C (SFH floor heating) / 45 C (MFH assumption), DHW 55 C;

Model M-001: Carnot-fraction heat-pump COP in CityLearn's functional form, and electricity -> heat derivation.

COP(T_out) = eta * (T_sup + 273.15) / (T_sup - T_out), values < 0 or > 20 set to 20
(identical to citylearn.energy_model.HeatPump.get_cop(heating=True), verified by a test).
Heat output of a mode = electricity * COP(T_out).  eta is calibrated so that the annual
ratio sum(heat)/sum(electricity) equals a target SPF (literature value, see parameter_registry.csv).

Task A6 / D-013: modeled hourly consumption-based LIFECYCLE carbon intensity of the Swiss electricity supply.

Inputs : data/raw/energy_charts/*.json (SRC-011, CC BY 4.0, attribution energy-charts.info):
         public_power for ch/de/fr/at/it (MW) and cbpf (cross-border physical flows into CH, GW; positive = import into CH,

R-001.title: `swiss.experiments.rewards.SwissDistrictReward` (D-019, accepted)
R-001.summary: reward_t = − Σ_k w_k · term_k(t) / scale_k, central agent, penalty-only.

fields.formula: reward_t = − Σ_k w_k · term_k(t) / scale_k, central agent, penalty-only.

terms.Unit: CHF per step (EKZ standard 2023, excl. VAT)
terms.Scale: mean per-step value under zero-action rollout

code.source:
Reward function R-001 for the Swiss heating district (Task A8, decision D-019).

Penalty-only, district level (central agent). Terms (each >= 0), each divided by a reference scale:
  cost   : sum_b max(net_b, 0) * electricity_pricing          [CHF per step]
  peak   : (max(sum_b net_b, 0))**2                           [kW^2, smooth surrogate of peak demand]
  ramp   : |sum_b net_b(t) - sum_b net_b(t-1)|                [kW]
  carbon : sum_b max(net_b, 0) * carbon_intensity             [only if the observation exists; weight 0 otherwise]
reward = - sum_k w_k * term_k / scale_k.   Scales = mean of each term under the uncontrolled (zero-action) rollout
(computed by run_baselines.py, stored in results/reward_scales.json).
A comfort term is deliberately ABSENT: the Phase A dataset has no thermal dynamics or measured indoor temperature, and
heating/DHW demand is always met, so a comfort penalty would be meaningless (D-018/D-019).

def terms(self, observations):
        net = np.array([o['net_electricity_consumption'] for o in observations], dtype=float)
        imp = np.maximum(net, 0.0)
        price = np.array([o['electricity_pricing'] for o in observations], dtype=float)
        district = float(net.sum())
        ramp = 0.0 if self._prev is None else abs(district - self._prev)
        self._prev = district
        carbon = 0.0
        if all('carbon_intensity' in o for o in observations):
            carbon = float((imp * np.array([o['carbon_intensity'] for o in observations], dtype=float)).sum())
        return {'cost': float((imp * price).sum()), 'peak': max(district, 0.0) ** 2, 'ramp': ramp, 'carbon': carbon}

series:carbon_intensity.title: Grid carbon intensity (modeled)
series:carbon_intensity.summary: MODELED, not measured. Hourly lifecycle CO2 intensity of the electricity used in Switzerland, rebuilt from Energy-Charts generation and cross-border flow data (M-002). The yearly mean is 58.1 g/kWh, but do not read the level: the proxy emission factors alone move that mean between 47 and 69 g/kWh, and the level is only about 61% to 62% of the EPFL reference. A method check against the EPFL 2016-17 series agrees in shape (hourly r 0.98) but not in level (ratio of means 0.61 in 2016, 0.62 in 2017). Use it for relative signals only (D-013b).

code.source:
def intensity(df, solar_ef, proxy_scale=1.0):
    ef = dict(EF_IPCC); ef.update({k: v * proxy_scale for k, v in EF_PROXY.items()}); ef['Solar'] = solar_ef
    # technologies that are entirely absent (all NaN for the whole window) are not part of that system's mix
    df = df.dropna(axis=1, how='all')
    df = df.apply(structural_zero)
    cols = [c for c in df.columns if c not in EXCLUDE and c in ef]
    unknown = [c for c in df.columns if c not in EXCLUDE and c not in ef]
    assert not unknown, f'unmapped technologies: {unknown}'
    g = df[cols].clip(lower=0)
    # NaN in any generation column makes the hour NaN (no interpolation)
    tot = g.sum(axis=1, min_count=len(cols))
    emis = (g * pd.Series(ef)[cols]).sum(axis=1, min_count=len(cols))
    return emis / tot, tot, emis

Task A6 / D-013: modeled hourly consumption-based LIFECYCLE carbon intensity of the Swiss electricity supply.

Inputs : data/raw/energy_charts/*.json (SRC-011, CC BY 4.0, attribution energy-charts.info):
         public_power for ch/de/fr/at/it (MW) and cbpf (cross-border physical flows into CH, GW; positive = import into CH,
         sign convention verified: July 2023 net export of 56 GWh/day equals ch 'Cross border electricity trading').
Method (first-order tracing, average not marginal intensity):
  I_dom,t = sum_k G_k,t EF_k / sum_k G_k,t                       (Swiss domestic generation only; diagnostic series)
  I_n,t   = same formula for neighbour n (FR, DE, AT, IT) from its own generation (its own imports ignored)
  I_cons,t = [sum_k G_k,t EF_k + sum_n max(F_n,t,0) * I_n,t] / [sum_k G_k,t + sum_n max(F_n,t,0)]
  Exports leave at the average mix (do not change the intensity). Pumped-storage generation and consumption are excluded.
Emission factors: IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III Table A.III.2 lifecycle medians (verified from the PDF) with documented PROXIES
for technologies absent from that table (see EF_PROXY). Output unit gCO2eq/kWh (and kg/kWh for CityLearn).
No interpolation: hours with missing inputs stay NaN and are counted.
Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_carbon.py [2023|2016|2017]

code.source:
def single_family():
    h = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(INT, 'heapo_candidates.csv'))
    pool = h[h.has_hp_submeter & (h.cov_2023 >= MIN_COV) & (h.cov_hp_2023 >= MIN_COV)
             & (h.Survey_HeatPump_Installation_Type == 'air-source')
             & (h.Survey_Building_Type == 'house') & h.Survey_Building_LivingArea.notna()
             & (h.n_dup_ts == 0)].copy()
    # three strata by terciles of 2023 heat-pump electricity
    q = pool.kwh_hp_2023.quantile([1 / 3, 2 / 3]).values
    pool['stratum'] = np.where(pool.kwh_hp_2023 <= q[0], 'low', np.where(pool.kwh_hp_2023 <= q[1], 'mid', 'high'))
    rows = []
    for s in ['low', 'mid', 'high']:
        r = nearest_to_median(pool[pool.stratum == s], 'kwh_hp_2023')
        rows.append({'role': f'SFH-{s}', 'source': 'HEAPO', 'id': int(r.Household_ID), 'stratum': s,
                     'n_pool': int((pool.stratum == s).sum()), 'kwh_total_2023': r.kwh_total_2023,
                     'kwh_hp_2023': r.kwh_hp_2023, 'area_m2': r.Survey_Building_LivingArea,
                     'residents': r.Survey_Building_Residents, 'pv_flag': r.Installation_HasPVSystem,
                     'units': 1})
    return rows, len(pool)

def multi_family():
    m = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(INT, 'ekz_meters.csv'))
    pool = m[(m['0_installation_type'] == 'Heat pump') & (m['0_object_type'] == 'Apartment building')

card:cop_model.title: Heat-pump COP and thermal demand
card:cop_model.summary: Heat delivered is not measured. It is derived from measured heat-pump electricity times a modeled COP whose Carnot fraction η is calibrated per building so the annual SPF matches Swiss field data (Arpagaus et al. 2023). The non-space-heating baseline of heat-pump electricity (warm-day mean, A-005) becomes the hot-water demand.

code.source:
def cop(t_out, eta, t_sup):
    t_out = np.asarray(t_out, dtype=float)
    with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
        c = eta * (t_sup + 273.15) / (t_sup - t_out)
    c = np.where(c < 0, 20.0, c)
    c = np.where(c > 20, 20.0, c)
    return c

def calibrate_eta(elec, t_out, t_sup, spf_target, lo=0.05, hi=1.0):
    """eta such that sum(elec*cop)/sum(elec) = spf_target (bisection; monotone in eta)."""
    elec = np.asarray(elec, dtype=float)
    m = ~(np.isnan(elec) | np.isnan(t_out))
    e, t = elec[m], np.asarray(t_out)[m]
    f = lambda eta: (e * cop(t, eta, t_sup)).sum() / e.sum() - spf_target
    if f(lo) > 0 or f(hi) < 0:
        raise ValueError('spf_target not reachable within eta bounds')
    for _ in range(80):
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        lo, hi = (mid, hi) if f(mid) < 0 else (lo, mid)
    return (lo + hi) / 2

def split_baseline(e_hp, local_hour, temp_c, warm_threshold_c=16.0):
    """Split hourly HP electricity into a non-space-heating baseline and space heating.

    Baseline per day B = mean daily electricity on days with mean T >= warm_threshold_c.
    Hourly shape p(h) = mean warm-day profile by local hour (normalised to sum 1).
    E_base(t) = min(E(t), B * p(hour(t))) ; E_sh = E - E_base.  Returns (e_base, e_sh, B_kwh_day).
    """
    import pandas as pd
    s = pd.Series(np.asarray(e_hp, dtype=float), index=e_hp.index)
    days = s.index.tz_convert('Europe/Zurich').floor('1D')
    tmean = pd.Series(np.asarray(temp_c, dtype=float), index=s.index).groupby(days).transform('mean')
    warm = (tmean >= warm_threshold_c).to_numpy()
    full = s.groupby(days).transform(lambda x: x.notna().all()).to_numpy().astype(bool)
    ok = warm & full
    B = float(s[ok].groupby(days[ok]).sum().mean())
    prof = s[ok].groupby(s.index.tz_convert('Europe/Zurich').hour[ok]).mean()
    prof = prof / prof.sum()
    hours = s.index.tz_convert('Europe/Zurich').hour
    base = np.minimum(s.to_numpy(), B * prof.reindex(hours).to_numpy())
    base = pd.Series(base, index=s.index)
    return base, s - base, B

def terms(self, observations):
        net = np.array([o['net_electricity_consumption'] for o in observations], dtype=float)
        imp = np.maximum(net, 0.0)
        price = np.array([o['electricity_pricing'] for o in observations], dtype=float)
        district = float(net.sum())
        ramp = 0.0 if self._prev is None else abs(district - self._prev)
        self._prev = district
        carbon = 0.0
        if all('carbon_intensity' in o for o in observations):
            carbon = float((imp * np.array([o['carbon_intensity'] for o in observations], dtype=float)).sum())
        return {'cost': float((imp * price).sum()), 'peak': max(district, 0.0) ** 2, 'ramp': ramp, 'carbon': carbon}

def terms(self, observations):
        net = np.array([o['net_electricity_consumption'] for o in observations], dtype=float)
        imp = np.maximum(net, 0.0)
        price = np.array([o['electricity_pricing'] for o in observations], dtype=float)
        district = float(net.sum())
        ramp = 0.0 if self._prev is None else abs(district - self._prev)
        self._prev = district
        carbon = 0.0
        if all('carbon_intensity' in o for o in observations):
            carbon = float((imp * np.array([o['carbon_intensity'] for o in observations], dtype=float)).sum())
        return {'cost': float((imp * price).sum()), 'peak': max(district, 0.0) ** 2, 'ramp': ramp, 'carbon': carbon}

card:district.title: The simulated district
card:district.summary: Six real buildings that are not neighbours: three single-family houses from HEAPO and three apartment buildings from EKZ, combined into one district (D-006) under one weather station (D-010). Heat pumps and their electricity are measured; heat demand is derived; tanks and the apartment loads are synthetic. The illustration shows one hour at a time for the controller selected in the header: cable and pipe animation speed and width follow that hour's electricity, tank fill shows state of charge, and the controller lines show whether it charges or discharges. Building height only reflects the number of housing units; the geometry is otherwise illustrative.
